feature: Several picked clips change track together
summary: Pick two or more clips and drag one of them up or down: they all go the same number of tracks and the same time, as one undo. Above the top track a new track is made for them, the way a single clip's drop makes one.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The walk is several-picked-clips-change-track-walk.

try.do: Open a screen recording, trim it to six seconds with W, then Sequence > Add Media at Playhead with the playhead at the end to put a second clip after it on V1.
Cut each clip once with Command K.
Click a piece of the first clip, then Command click a piece of the second.
Drag the second clip a little right and up past the top of V1, and watch the line over V1 and the readout.
Let go: both clips sit on a new V2, a little later, cuts and sound intact.
Press Command Z once: both are back on V1 and V2 is gone.
Pick both again and drag one down onto the Audio track: the lane lights red.
Let go: both stay on V1 and only slide in time.

evaluate: When you carry several clips up, is the line over the top track enough to tell you all of them are going, not just the one in your hand?
Does one Command Z undoing the whole move, new track included, match what you expect from Premiere?
When the move is refused, is sliding in time anyway what you want, or would you rather nothing moved at all?
With clips on two tracks picked, does each one going up by the same count feel right?
rough: While in the hand only the lane under the pointer lights up; the other picked clips do not show where they will land until you let go. The single clip drop works the same way.
A refusal because the track takes only sound reads "no room on Audio", the single clip's words; task a-clip-refused-by-a-track-of-the-wrong-kind-says gives it the real reason.

Tracks are counted down the whole list, so a pick that mixes picture with a separate music clip refuses to go up (the music would land on a picture track). Premiere moves sound the other way instead; not built.
Option dragging several picked clips still leaves copies on their own tracks and only slides them in time.
The walk puts the second clip on the timeline by dropping the file there, not through Add Media at Playhead, because the menu step needs the Mac to itself.
No mock frame draws several clips carried between tracks; the cues are the ones the single clip drop already uses.
